technical.summary: Mixed momentum setup with bullish short-term indicators (RSI14 rising, AO cross-up, OBV rising) conflicted by overbought conditions (Stoch, Williams %R) and price below intermediate moving averages; moderate confluence but elevated risk of pullback.

fundamental.summary: CMG shows no insider buying conviction, no institutional accumulation signal, zero government contracts, no lobbying activity, minimal retail interest, and elevated earnings risk with 71 days to next report.

sentiment.summary: Weak congressional selling pressure combined with extreme fear sentiment (28/100) presents a contrarian buy setup, though absence of recent news data limits conviction.

risk.summary: Extreme VIX crisis regime (372.96) dominates risk assessment; normal yield curve provides limited offset; earnings in 71 days adds moderate event risk to discretionary consumer sector.

debate.key_bull_argument: RSI14 rising, AO cross-up, and OBV rising provide short-term momentum confirmation, with extreme fear sentiment (28/100) and contrarian buy signal offering asymmetric risk/reward if panic reverses.
debate.key_bear_argument: Overbought stochastic/Williams %R conditions, price below both 50-day moving averages, Ichimoku below cloud, VIX crisis regime (372.96), zero fundamental conviction, and 71-day earnings event risk create a high-probability pullback setup that negates technical momentum.

decision.entry_rationale: Technical momentum (RSI rising, AO cross-up, OBV rising) and extreme fear sentiment (28/100) offer contrarian appeal, but overbought conditions and price below 50-day MAs signal weak entry quality.
decision.primary_risk: VIX crisis regime (372.96) combined with overbought stochastic/Williams %R creates high probability of sharp pullback before momentum can extend; 71-day earnings event adds discretionary sector event risk.
decision.agent_agreement: strong — all agents aligned on bear case dominance
decision.portfolio_note: Already holding CMG position with 35 existing Consumer Discretionary positions (12% of portfolio); concentration risk and sector saturation argue against adding exposure.
